title: Microsoft Purview: Rights Management connector moves to certificate-based authentication
summary: The briefing passes: its planned authentication changes and target dates match the roadmap, and its existing connector administration guidance is supported by Microsoft Learn. Searches confirmed that connector-specific certificate configuration, migration behaviour and pricing remain undocumented.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this connector authentication change.
claims.quote: Searched: "RMS connector" "certificate-based authentication". Opened Deploying and Installing and configuring the Microsoft Rights Management connector; results described existing setup, HTTPS or unrelated products.

claims.claim: Learn's existing installation procedure requires an administrator to sign in.
claims.quote: Select Sign In to sign in to your account. Make sure you enter credentials for an account that has sufficient privileges to configure the RMS connector.

claims.claim: The existing installer sets up security tokens for the connector.
claims.quote: Azure RMS is also prepared for configuration by creating the following: ... A set of security tokens for the connector, which authorize operations with Azure RMS.

claims.claim: The existing connector's security tokens are stored in the local registry.
claims.quote: These tokens are downloaded from Azure RMS and installed on the local computer in the registry.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The existing connector creates a Microsoft Entra service principal named Aadrm_S-1-7-0.
claims.quote: The service principal account in Microsoft Entra ID, Aadrm_S-1-7-0, that the connector creates.

claims.claim: The connector supports Exchange Server, SharePoint Server and Windows file servers using File Classification Infrastructure (FCI).
claims.quote: This connector provides data protection for existing on-premises deployments that use Microsoft Exchange Server, SharePoint Server, or file servers that run Windows Server and File Classification Infrastructure (FCI).

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The connector acts as a relay between on-premises servers and Azure Rights Management.
claims.quote: After you deploy the connector, it acts as a communications interface (a relay) between the on-premises servers and the cloud service

claims.claim: The connector credential authorizes its operations against Azure RMS.
claims.quote: A set of security tokens for the connector, which authorize operations with Azure RMS.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the default arrival behaviour of certificate-based connector authentication.
claims.quote: Searched: "Rights Management connector" "certificate" "default" "existing" migration. Read the roadmap and opened Deploying and Installing and configuring the Microsoft Rights Management connector; no arrival default for the new authentication was stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated what this authentication change does to connectors that are already installed.
claims.quote: Searched: "Rights Management connector" "certificate" "default" "existing" migration. Opened Installing and configuring the Microsoft Rights Management connector; its update guidance did not cover this change.

claims.claim: No source states that existing connector behaviour changes before the January CY2027 target.
claims.quote: Searched: "Rights Management connector" "certificate" "default" "existing" migration. Read the roadmap and opened Deploying and Installing and configuring the Microsoft Rights Management connector; no earlier change to existing installations was stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Accounts specified for the Exchange Server role in connector configuration receive the Azure RMS super user role.
claims.quote: All accounts that you specify for the Exchange Server role in the connector configuration are granted the super user role in Azure RMS

claims.claim: The Azure RMS super user role grants those accounts access to all content for the RMS tenant.
claims.quote: which gives them access to all content for this RMS tenant.

claims.quote: With this update, administrators configure their own Microsoft Entra app registration and certificate, then use the new PowerShell module to configure the certificate for each workload (Connector, Exchange, SharePoint, and FCI).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published the permissions required by the new connector app registration.
claims.quote: Searched: "Rights Management connector" "app registration" permissions module upgrade existing. Read connector installation and Connect-AipService excerpts; the latter covers service administration, not the new connector.

claims.claim: Learn says the account installing and configuring the existing connector must not require MFA.
claims.quote: The Rights Management connector and the Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner don't support MFA. If you deploy the connector or scanner, the following accounts mustn't require MFA: ... The account that installs and configures the connector.

claims.claim: Learn says the existing connector's Aadrm_S-1-7-0 service principal must not require MFA.
claims.quote: If you deploy the connector or scanner, the following accounts mustn't require MFA: ... The service principal account in Microsoft Entra ID, Aadrm_S-1-7-0, that the connector creates.

claims.claim: Learn requires at least two connector computers for fault tolerance.
claims.quote: For fault tolerance and high availability, you must install the RMS connector on a minimum of two computers.

claims.claim: The authentication option is treated as included under the Azure Rights Management service's existing subscription entitlement.
claims.quote: Use the Azure Rights Management service with Microsoft 365 subscriptions or subscriptions for Microsoft Purview Information Protection.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Learn says to use Azure Rights Management with Microsoft 365 subscriptions or subscriptions for Microsoft Purview Information Protection.
claims.quote: Use the Azure Rights Management service with Microsoft 365 subscriptions or subscriptions for Microsoft Purview Information Protection.

claims.claim: The connector deployment page names no separate connector licence among its prerequisites.
claims.quote: Prerequisites for the RMS connector: The protection service is activated; Directory synchronization between your on-premises Active Directory forests and Microsoft Entra ID; A minimum of two member computers on which to install the RMS connector; TLS version 1.2.

claims.quote: Searched: "Rights Management connector" "certificate" "license" "pricing". Opened connector deployment and Azure Rights Management overview and requirements; no feature-specific price appeared.

claims.claim: No meter specific to certificate-based connector authentication is published at the time of writing.

claims.quote: Searched: "Rights Management connector" "certificate" "license" "pricing". Opened connector deployment and Azure Rights Management overview; existing service subscriptions, not a new authentication licence, were stated.

claims.claim: Today's installing account may be a tenant global administrator.
claims.quote: Global administrator for your tenant: An account that is a global administrator for your Microsoft 365 tenant or Microsoft Entra tenant.

claims.claim: Today's installing account may be an Azure Rights Management global administrator.
claims.quote: Azure Rights Management global administrator: An account in Microsoft Entra ID that has been assigned the Azure RMS global administrator role.

claims.claim: Today's installing account may be an Azure Rights Management connector administrator authorized to install and administer the connector.
claims.quote: Azure Rights Management connector administrator: An account in Microsoft Entra ID that has been granted rights to install and administer the RMS connector for your organization.

claims.claim: If onboarding controls are implemented, the installing account must be allowed to protect content.
claims.quote: If you have implemented onboarding controls, make sure that the account you specify is able to protect content.

claims.claim: When protection is restricted to a group, the installing account must belong to that permitted group.
claims.quote: For example, if you restricted the ability to protect content to the "IT department" group, the account that you specify here must be a member of that group.

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra's Application Administrator role can create and manage app registrations.
claims.quote: Users in this role can create and manage all aspects of enterprise applications, application registrations, and application proxy settings.

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra's Application Administrator role can manage application credentials.
claims.quote: This role grants the ability to manage application credentials. Users assigned this role can add credentials to an application, and use those credentials to impersonate the application's identity.

claims.claim: Connector-specific authorization for the new PowerShell module is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Rights Management connector" "app registration" permissions module upgrade existing. Opened connector installation and read AIPService reference excerpts; no authorization requirements for the new module appeared.

claims.claim: The existing delegated connector administrator role has no documented management-portal configuration surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "RMS connector" "ConnectorAdministrator" management portal delegated administration. Opened connector installation and Add-AipServiceRoleBasedAdministrator: delegated administrative configuration must use PowerShell, not a management portal.

claims.claim: Add-AipServiceRoleBasedAdministrator -EmailAddress <email address> -Role ConnectorAdministrator assigns the existing connector administrator role using AIPService PowerShell.
claims.quote: Add-AipServiceRoleBasedAdministrator [-EmailAddress <String>] [-Role <Role>]; ConnectorAdministrator; the account is granted least privileges to configure and run the Rights Management (RMS) connector.

claims.claim: Neither an admin UI nor a command is yet documented for configuring the new certificate-based authentication for the connector and its workloads.
claims.quote: Searched: "RMS connector" "certificate-based authentication"; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/aipservice "connector" "certificate". Read connector installation and AIPService excerpts; neither documents the planned workload authentication control.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The roadmap description specifies administrator authentication and configuration changes, not new autonomous actions or end-user behaviour.
claims.quote: New PowerShell cmdlets handle certificate import, registry configuration, private-key permissions, and validation. ... Customers should plan to register an Entra ID application and upload a certificate before installing or upgrading the connector.
